body.statement: Under cohort overlap, exactly two latent types, consistency, type-conditional first-order Markov paths, and four-slice rank, every cohort and type has positive active mass: for all \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(j\in\{1,2\}\), \(\alpha_j^d>0\).  Consequently \(\pi_j^d\geq\alpha_j^d>0\), so cohort-specific type overlap is implied rather than separately assumed.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  Cohort overlap makes conditioning on \(D=d\) well defined.  Consistency and the type-conditional first-order Markov property imply that, for every \(x,y,u,v\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 \bar A_{xy}^d[u,v]
 =\sum_{j=1}^2
 P(Z=j,X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d)\,
 P(X_2=y\mid X_1=x,Z=j,D=d)\,
 P(X_3=v\mid X_2=y,Z=j,D=d).                            \tag{14}
\]
For fixed \((x,y,d)\), each summand in \((14)\) is an outer product of a two-vector indexed by \(u\) and a two-vector indexed by \(v\), multiplied by the scalar middle transition probability.  Suppose \(\alpha_{j_0}^d=0\) for one type \(j_0\).  By the definition of \(\alpha_{j_0}^d\),
\[
 P(Z=j_0,X_1=x\mid D=d)=0\qquad(x\in\mathcal A),        \tag{15}
\]
so every first factor for type \(j_0\) in \((14)\) is zero.  Because there are exactly two types, \((14)\) then contains at most one nonzero outer product.  Hence \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar A_{xy}^d)\leq1\), contradicting the assumed positive smallest singular value of each \(2\times2\) matrix \(\bar A_{xy}^d\).  Thus \(\alpha_j^d>0\) for both types.  Finally,
\[
 \pi_j^d=P(Z=j\mid D=d)
 \geq P(Z=j,X_1\in\mathcal A\mid D=d)=\alpha_j^d>0.      \tag{16}
\]
Since \(d\) was arbitrary, the conclusion holds in both cohorts.
